OptionsMenu

The OptionsMenu control displays a list of choices. Each choice is a MenuItem containing its label, callback and enabled state.

Properties and Methods

  • Options: The List<MenuItem> displayed by the menu. MenuItem objects go in this property rather than Children.
  • MenuItem.Option / OnSelect / IsEnabled: Option is the label, OnSelect is the Action to call, and IsEnabled controls whether the item can be selected.
  • SelectedIndex: The current selection. This is -1 when the menu is empty, and is adjusted when the options change.
  • MenuName / SelectedForeground / SelectedBackground: MenuName is the heading displayed inside the menu. The color properties control the selected item.

C# Example

Create the control and add it to the page's Children or the window's Elements collection. The Controls Overview lists the namespaces used by these examples.

MXML Example

App refers to the SettingsModel backend from the Data Binding Guide. Register it with page.BackendObjects.Add("App", model) before compiling.

Output Example

Keyboard Controls

  • Up / Down: Wrap through enabled choices.
  • Home / End, PageUp / PageDown: Navigate to an edge or scroll by a page.
  • Enter / Right: Activate the selected item.
  • Letters / digits: Cycle matching caption prefixes.

Notes

You can add or remove options while the menu is in use, including leaving it empty. Change the list on the UI thread while the control is attached.

MenuItem is a data object, not a UIElement. Its OnSelect callback takes no parameters and runs on the UI thread.

The common position, color, visibility and lifetime settings are inherited from UIElement. While attached to a running window, update the control on the UI thread.
